videos.content: Screen recording of a PUBLIC YouTube video (Jay Harris, 'Basic ASL Conversation'), two signers. Clip covers video 0:03-0:19 = greeting lines 1-6 only.
videos.notes: WARNING: greetings are the highest-prior exchange in ASL. A VLM emits 'Hello / How are you? / I'm fine' for any two-signer clip without decoding anything, so this scores ~65% by guessing. The DIAGNOSTIC content is lines 7-11 (deaf/hearing), which are NOT in this clip. Nine machine runs across 5 configs are tabulated in curify-studio/docs/asl-recognition-evaluation-2026-08-18.md section 3; none are in projectsegment.

Longest job in the set. Budget-implied sampling density 1 frame / 3.13s. Output is the most fluent and most confident in the corpus AND the most likely to be fabricated — the 'priors dominate when perception is weak' failure mode.

videos.gt_kind: BURNED-IN ENGLISH CAPTIONS — extractable ground truth, not yet transcribed
videos.content: Professionally produced ASL video: single signer, plain grey studio background, title card reading 'INSTRUCTION', English captions burned into the frame throughout. Sampled caption lines: 'What if you could have a positive relationship?' / 'Happiness comes from our hearts and our lives.' / 'The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.' / "I'm not happy; I'm just trying to find a few things."
videos.notes: MISFILED, and confirmed ASL by frame inspection on 2026-08-25 (was listed as unconfirmed before that). HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM IN THE CORPUS: studio-quality, single signer, face fully visible, and it carries its own aligned English ground truth on screen. OCR the caption band to get a free labelled ASL->English pair. Verify direction of production (ASL rendition captioned vs. English source interpreted) before treating captions as a gold translation.

input_mask.reason: English captions burned into the frame for ~69% of the clip; title cards additionally leak the topic ('CATEGORY: RELIGIOUS') and the exercise instructions.
input_mask.method: Unconditional ffmpeg drawbox over the caption band (y=795 h=155, full width, ALL frames), plus full-frame black over the two title/instruction cards (t<15.0 and t>132.1, the ranges where the signer is absent). Re-encoded libx264 crf 18; duration and frame count unchanged.
input_mask.verified: Exhaustive, every frame, not sampled: the band is fully black in 4112 of 4112 frames (ffmpeg crop of the band -> 16x4 gray -> max pixel < 10). Card ranges confirmed black. Sampled OCR is NOT sufficient to verify this and was wrong when tried.
input_mask.why_unconditional: Masking only the frames where a caption was detected was tried first and rejected: OCR-derived intervals left 14 gaps totalling ~22s in which captions were still on screen, and a sampled OCR sweep failed to notice. Unconditional masking is verifiable in one exhaustive pass and cannot have holes. Measured cost of always-on masking: 8 frames (0.3s of 137s) where the signer's hands are in the band during active signing -- everywhere else her hands are in the band only at rest, and during captioned frames the caption box already occluded that region.
input_mask.signal_cost: 0.3s of active signing occluded (8 of 4112 frames)

videos.production_direction: RESOLVED 2026-08-30 by OCR of the title cards: 'Certificate Program for Sign Language Interpreters — RECEPTIVE SKILLS EVALUATION', 'SIGN TO VOICE', 'Record yourself voicing the video'. This is an interpreter certification exercise, so the ASL is the SOURCE and the burned captions are the answer key — a reference English rendering of the signing. That is the direction the candidate reference needs in order to be usable as gold.

determinism_pair.what_happened: The same video was submitted by two different accounts 11 seconds apart and processed as two independent production jobs.
determinism_pair.identity_evidence: Identical duration to the millisecond (189.504000s), identical codec/resolution/framerate, identical frame counts (5684 video / 8884 audio), file sizes differ by 0.02% (49,304,806 vs 49,314,506 bytes) — independently re-encoded on upload. Frames sampled at t=30s, 90s and 150s are visually identical.
determinism_pair.interpretation: Segmentation (the motion-energy sampler) is deterministic; recognition (the VLM) is not. Free production A/B on identical input. Both submitters were charged 32 credits.
determinism_pair.caveat: Decode temperature is unset in _call_vlm, so Gemini defaults to 1.0. Pin temperature=0 before attributing any of this variance to the model's ASL competence.

baseline0_config.pipeline: motion-energy probe -> active/idle run segmentation -> 100% of budget allocated inside active runs -> ffmpeg stills at 512px -> N batched VLM calls -> JSON segments
